title: iManageParkinson – Feasibility Study on the Collection and Analysis of Patient-Generated Symptom Diary and Self-Test Data Over the Course of Parkinson’s Disease
summary: In Parkinson's disease, symptoms fluctuate during the day, for example depending on medication timing, which is hard to capture during clinic visits. This study tests whether people with Parkinson's can reliably record their symptoms, medication and meals with a smartphone diary and complete short tasks such as speaking, finger tapping and a reaction task. Up to 50 participants will use the app for about three weeks, with no change to their treatment. We will examine whether symptom fluctuations can be made visible and whether the data are suitable for computer-assisted analysis, to help tailor medication adjustment to individual patients in the long term.

interventions.name: There is no intervention or control group; instead, there is a single observational group consisting of up to 50 adult Parkinson’s patients on long-term dopaminergic medication, who are recruited through the study center’s neurology department and the self-help group Jung & Parkinson e.V. Following

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Diagnosed Parkinson's disease with ongoing dopaminergic medication
• Ownership of a suitable smartphone and basic smartphone proficiency
• The patient is not under the care of a caregiver and is able to understand the study informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
• Suicidal tendencies, psychosis
• Other comorbidities that may interfere with the study treatment and compromise the interpretation of the study results
